traditions.name: Rabbinic Judaism (Talmud / Midrash)
traditions.scholarly_note: Distinct from the Hebrew Bible layer (hebrew-ot) and from medieval Kabbalah; covers named angelology and demonology of Talmud, Targum and Midrash.

traditions.name: Mandaeism (Nasoraean)
traditions.earliest_attestation: c. 1st–3rd c. CE (debated); manuscripts from 16th c., incantation bowls c. 5th–7th c.
traditions.scholarly_note: Last surviving ancient Gnostic religion; origins in the Jordan region are claimed by the tradition (Haran Gawaita) and debated by historians.

traditions.name: Yazidism (Êzidî)
traditions.earliest_attestation: 12th c. CE (Sheikh ʿAdī ibn Musāfir, d. 1162) with older Iranian substrate
traditions.scholarly_note: Transmitted chiefly through oral hymns (qewls); the so-called Black Book and Book of Revelation (Kitab al-Jilwa) published in the early 20th c. are of disputed authenticity.

traditions.name: Druze (al-Muwaḥḥidūn)
traditions.scholarly_note: Grew out of Ismaili Shiʿism; the Daʿwa was closed to new members in 1043.

traditions.name: Samaritanism
traditions.scholarly_note: Holds the Samaritan Pentateuch as sole scripture; claims to preserve the original Israelite religion.

traditions.name: Rastafari
traditions.earliest_attestation: 1930s CE (after the coronation of Haile Selassie I, 1930)

traditions.name: LaVeyan Satanism (Church of Satan)
traditions.scholarly_note: Founded by Anton Szandor LaVey; atheistic, Satan as symbol.

traditions.name: Theistic Satanism
traditions.scholarly_note: An umbrella for groups that venerate Satan as a real being; heterogeneous, no single founder or text.

traditions.name: Luciferianism
traditions.scholarly_note: Modern current venerating Lucifer as light-bringer and liberator; overlaps with, but often distinguishes itself from, Satanism.

traditions.name: Temple of Set
traditions.scholarly_note: Founded by Michael Aquino after leaving the Church of Satan; theistic Left-Hand Path initiatory order.

traditions.name: The Satanic Temple
traditions.scholarly_note: Non-theistic religious and activist organisation; Satan as literary symbol.

traditions.name: Western Occultism (19th-c. ritual magic)
traditions.scholarly_note: Covers occult figures created or reshaped by 19th-c. magicians that later traditions inherited.

traditions.name: Thelema
traditions.earliest_attestation: 1904 CE (reception of The Book of the Law, Cairo)
traditions.scholarly_note: Founded by Aleister Crowley; organised later through the A∴A∴ and Ordo Templi Orientis.

traditions.name: Wicca / modern Paganism
traditions.scholarly_note: Modern revival religion; its claim of continuity with an ancient witch-cult is rejected by historians, though many practitioners now treat it as mythic rather than historical.

traditions.name: Unitarian Christianity
traditions.geographic_origin: Poland, Transylvania; later Britain and New England

traditions.name: Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Christianity
traditions.earliest_attestation: 4th c. CE (conversion of King Ezana of Aksum)
traditions.scholarly_note: Its canon uniquely includes 1 Enoch and Jubilees.

deities.etymology: Hebrew śāṭān, 'adversary, accuser, one who obstructs'; verb śṭn 'to oppose, accuse'.
deities.summary: The satan is a member of the heavenly court, one of the bene ha-elohim who present themselves before YHWH. He roams the earth and tests the righteousness of Job with God's permission, stands at the right hand of the high priest Joshua to accuse him, and in Chronicles rises against Israel and moves David to take a census. He has no power of his own: every trial he brings is licensed by the Lord.

deities.etymology: Hebrew mî-kā-ʾēl, 'Who is like God?'
deities.summary: Michael is "one of the chief princes", the great prince who stands guard over Israel. He comes to the aid of the angel sent to Daniel against the prince of Persia, and at the end of days he will arise in a time of trouble when the people are delivered and the dead awake.

deities.etymology: Hebrew gavrî-ʾēl, 'God is my strength' or 'man of God'.
deities.summary: Gabriel is the angel who comes "in swift flight" to make Daniel understand his visions, explaining the vision of the ram and the goat and revealing the seventy weeks. In Enoch he is one of the four great angels who bring the cry of the earth before God.

The Angel of the LORD speaks as God and in God's name: he finds Hagar in the wilderness, stays Abraham's hand at Moriah, appears in the burning bush, and goes before Israel, for "my Name is in him". Those who see him fear they have seen God.

deities.etymology: Hebrew liwyātān, from lwy 'to coil, twist'; cognate with Ugaritic ltn (Litan/Lotan).
deities.summary: Leviathan is the many-headed sea dragon whom God crushed at the beginning, giving its flesh as food to the wilderness people, and whom God will punish "on that day" with his great sword. In Job he is the untameable beast no human can hook; in the Psalms God formed him to play in the sea. Later tradition reserves his flesh for the banquet of the righteous in the world to come.

alternate_names: First of the Ways of God
deities.etymology: Hebrew bəhēmôt, intensive plural of bəhēmâ 'beast' — 'the Beast par excellence'.
deities.summary: Behemoth is the first of God's works, a land-beast of immense strength whose bones are tubes of bronze; only his maker can approach him with a sword. Enoch makes him the male monster of the desert Dendain, paired with Leviathan, the female monster of the deep.

deities.etymology: Hebrew rahav, 'storming, arrogance'; unrelated to Rahab of Jericho (rāḥāb, different spelling).
deities.summary: Rahab is the raging sea power whom God cut to pieces and pierced at creation; her helpers bowed beneath him. The prophets turn her name into a byword for Egypt, the proud power God humbled at the Sea.

deities.etymology: Hebrew hêlēl 'shining one' (root hll 'to shine'); šaḥar 'dawn', also the name of the Ugaritic dawn god.
deities.summary: "How you have fallen from heaven, Shining One, son of Dawn!" The taunt over the king of Babylon tells of one who said in his heart: I will ascend to heaven, set my throne above the stars of El, sit on the mount of assembly in the far reaches of Zaphon, and make myself like the Most High — and who was brought down to Sheol, to the depths of the pit.

deities.etymology: Ugaritic ltn, vocalisation uncertain (Litan / Lôtan); from lwy 'to coil'.
deities.summary: Litan is the fleeing serpent, the twisting serpent, the tyrant with seven heads. Mot reminds Baal that he struck down Litan, and Anat boasts that she too crushed the twisting dragon, the mighty one of seven heads, among the allies of Prince Yam.

deities.etymology: Hebrew Baʿal Zəvûv 'lord of flies'; probably a pun on Ugaritic/Canaanite zbl bʿl 'Baal the Prince / Exalted Lord'.
deities.summary: Baal Zebub is the god of the Philistine city of Ekron, whose oracle King Ahaziah of Israel sent to consult when he lay injured. He is a lord who answers those who seek him about sickness and recovery.

deities.etymology: Hebrew mōlek: consonants of melek 'king', probably vocalised with the vowels of bōšet 'shame'.
deities.summary: Molech is the king to whom children were "passed through the fire" at the Topheth in the Valley of Hinnom. The Law forbids giving one's offspring to him, and Josiah defiled the Topheth so that none could make a son or daughter pass through the fire to Molech.

primary_sources: KTU 1.23 (The Birth of the Gracious Gods)
deities.etymology: Ugaritic šḥr 'dawn' (Hebrew šaḥar).
deities.summary: Shahar, Dawn, is born to El together with his twin Shalim, Dusk, the gracious and beautiful gods whose mouths reach from earth to heaven. He is the light that opens each day.

deities.etymology: Semitic ʿṯtr, cognate with Akkadian Ištar and Phoenician ʿAštart (Astarte), here a male deity.
deities.summary: When Baal lay dead, El and Athirat set Athtar the Terrible on Baal's throne on the heights of Zaphon. But his feet did not reach the footstool and his head did not reach the top; he declared "I cannot be king on the heights of Zaphon," came down from the throne, and ruled over the earth below instead.

alternate_names: Prince of the Dominion of Wickedness
deities.etymology: Hebrew bəliyyaʿal 'worthlessness' (bəlî 'without' + yaʿal 'worth'), used of scoundrels before it became a proper name.
deities.summary: Belial is the angel of hostility, created by God for the pit, who leads the Sons of Darkness and the spirits of his lot. In this age of wickedness he is let loose against Israel with three nets — fornication, wealth and defilement of the sanctuary — but at the final war God and the Sons of Light will destroy his dominion forever.

deities.etymology: Hebrew maśṭēmâ 'hostility', from the same root śṭm/śṭn as śāṭān.
deities.summary: When Noah prayed for the evil spirits to be bound, Mastema, chief of the spirits, begged God to leave him a tenth of them to do his will, and God granted it. Mastema provoked God to test Abraham with Isaac, sought to kill Moses on his way to Egypt, and strengthened Pharaoh's magicians — but always within the bounds God allows.

deities.etymology: Hebrew rəfāʾ-ʾēl, 'God heals'.
deities.summary: Raphael is one of the seven holy angels who stand before the glory of the Lord. Disguised as the kinsman Azarias he guides young Tobias, binds the demon Asmodeus and heals Tobit's blindness; in Enoch God sends him to bind Azazel hand and foot in the desert and to heal the earth the Watchers corrupted.

deities.earliest_attestation: c. 3rd c. BCE (Astronomical Book of Enoch)
deities.etymology: Hebrew ʾûrî-ʾēl, 'God is my light'.
deities.summary: Uriel is set over the luminaries of heaven and over Tartarus. He shows Enoch the laws of the sun, moon and stars and the reckoning of the year, guides him through the prisons of the fallen, and in 4 Ezra answers the seer's questions about the justice of God.

deities.etymology: Generally derived from Avestan aēšma-daēva, 'demon of wrath' (Middle Persian Xešm).
deities.summary: Asmodeus, the evil demon, loved Sarah and killed each of her seven husbands on the wedding night, until Raphael taught Tobias to drive him off with the smoke of a fish's heart and liver; the demon fled to Upper Egypt where Raphael bound him. The rabbis remember Ashmedai as king of demons, captured by Solomon to help build the Temple.

deities.earliest_attestation: c. 2nd c. CE (Ascension of Isaiah); rabbinic texts 3rd–9th c. CE
primary_sources: Treatise on the Left Emanation (R. Isaac ha-Kohen)
deities.etymology: Commonly read as sam-ʾēl 'poison of God'; the Gnostic Hypostasis of the Archons glosses it 'god of the blind' (Aramaic samya 'blind').
deities.summary: Samael was the great prince in heaven, with twelve wings. When God made Adam, Samael took his band, came down, and chose the serpent as his mount to lead Eve astray. He is the wicked one, chief of all the satans, and the angel of death who waits to take each soul. In the Kabbalah he is lord of the Other Side, and Lilith is his mate.

deities.etymology: Greek synadelphos 'co-brother', i.e. the brother of Metatron.
deities.summary: Sandalphon stands on the earth while his head reaches the living creatures of the Chariot; he is taller than his fellows by a journey of five hundred years. He stands behind the Chariot binding crowns for his Creator out of the prayers of Israel.

deities.etymology: Greek Satanas from Hebrew/Aramaic śāṭān 'adversary'; 'devil' from Greek diabolos 'slanderer', the Septuagint rendering of śāṭān.
deities.summary: Satan is the Devil, a murderer from the beginning and the father of lies, who tempted Christ in the wilderness and prowls like a roaring lion seeking whom he may devour. Once a glorious angel, he fell through pride and drew a third of the stars of heaven with him. He is the god of this age, disguising himself as an angel of light, but Christ has disarmed him on the cross; he will be bound and finally cast into the lake of fire.

deities.earliest_attestation: c. 382–405 CE (Vulgate, Isaiah 14:12); applied to Satan from the 3rd c. CE
deities.etymology: Latin lux 'light' + ferre 'to bear', rendering Greek Heōsphoros and Hebrew hêlēl.
deities.summary: Lucifer is the name of Satan before his fall: the brightest of the angels, the light-bearer and son of the morning, who said in his heart "I will be like the Most High" and was cast down from heaven to the depths of the pit. The fathers read Isaiah's fallen Day Star and Ezekiel's anointed cherub of Eden as his story.

deities.etymology: From Baal Zebub of Ekron (2 Kings 1) and/or zbl bʿl 'Baal the Prince'; Gospel manuscripts vary between Beelzeboul and Beelzebub.
deities.summary: Beelzebul is the prince of demons. When Jesus cast out demons his opponents said he did it by Beelzebul; Jesus answered that if Satan casts out Satan his kingdom cannot stand, and that he binds the strong man and plunders his house.

deities.earliest_attestation: 1st c. CE (New Testament); creedal definition 381 CE
deities.etymology: Greek pneuma hagion and Latin spiritus sanctus, translating Hebrew rûaḥ ha-qōdeš; rûaḥ means wind, breath and spirit.
deities.summary: The Holy Spirit is the third person of the Holy Trinity, the Lord and Giver of Life, who proceeds from the Father and with the Father and the Son is worshipped and glorified, and who spoke through the prophets. He descended on Christ at the Jordan as a dove and on the apostles at Pentecost as tongues of fire; he is the Paraclete who abides with the faithful and leads them into all truth.

deities.etymology: Hebrew mî-kā-ʾēl 'Who is like God?'
deities.summary: Michael is the prince of the heavenly host who waged war in heaven against the dragon and cast him and his angels down to earth. He disputed with the Devil over the body of Moses, defends the Church in battle, and weighs souls and leads them to judgment.

Gabriel, who stands in the presence of God, announced to Zechariah the birth of John and to the Virgin Mary that she would conceive the Son of the Most High: "Hail, full of grace, the Lord is with you."

Before the end the man of lawlessness will be revealed, who exalts himself above every so-called god and takes his seat in God's temple. The beast rising from the sea with ten horns and seven heads receives his power from the dragon and is worshipped by the nations, while the beast from the earth works signs on his behalf and marks his followers with his number, 666 — until Christ destroys him with the breath of his mouth.

deities.earliest_attestation: 1st c. CE (Revelation); as a place, Hebrew Bible
deities.etymology: Hebrew ʾăbaddôn 'destruction' (root ʾbd 'to perish'); Greek Apollyōn 'destroyer'.
deities.summary: When the fifth trumpet sounds, the shaft of the abyss is opened and locusts like war-horses come out to torment those without the seal of God. Their king is the angel of the bottomless pit, whose name in Hebrew is Abaddon and in Greek Apollyon, the Destroyer.

deities.earliest_attestation: 2nd c. CE (Basilides as reported by Irenaeus); magical gems 2nd–4th c. CE
primary_sources: Gospel of the Egyptians (NHC III,2; IV,2)
deities.etymology: Unknown; the isopsephic value Α-Β-Ρ-Α-Σ-Α-Ξ = 1+2+100+1+200+1+60 = 365.
deities.summary: Abrasax is the ruler of the three hundred and sixty-five heavens, for the letters of his name add up to 365, the days of the year. He holds the whole cycle of the heavens together and is invoked as a mighty name of power.

alternate_names: Rūḥ al-Qudus (the Holy Spirit, per most exegetes)
deities.etymology: Arabic form of Hebrew Gavriʾel.
iconography: Not depicted: Sunni and most Islamic practice is aniconic for prophets and angels; represented by calligraphy of the name
deities.summary: Jibrīl is the noblest of the angels, the Trustworthy Spirit who brought the Qurʾān down upon the heart of the Prophet Muḥammad by God's permission. He appeared to the Prophet on the horizon, came to teach the believers their religion — islām, īmān and iḥsān — and accompanied him on the Night Journey.

deities.etymology: Arabic form of Hebrew Mikhaʾel.
iconography: Not depicted: Sunni and most Islamic practice is aniconic for prophets and angels; represented by calligraphy of the name
deities.summary: Mīkāʾīl is one of the angels brought near, named in the Qurʾān beside Jibrīl: whoever is an enemy to God, His angels, His messengers, Jibrīl and Mīkāl, God is an enemy to the disbelievers. He is entrusted with the rain and the sustenance of creation.

deities.earliest_attestation: 7th–9th c. CE (named in ḥadīth; the Trumpet in the Qurʾān)
deities.etymology: Uncertain; sometimes connected with Hebrew śərāfîm (seraphim) or Raphael — both conjectural.
iconography: Not depicted: Sunni and most Islamic practice is aniconic for prophets and angels; represented by calligraphy of the name
deities.summary: Isrāfīl holds the Trumpet to his lips, waiting for the command. At the first blast all in the heavens and the earth will swoon; at the second they will rise, standing and looking on, for the Day of Resurrection.

deities.earliest_attestation: 7th c. CE (Angel of Death in the Qurʾān); name later
iconography: Not depicted: Sunni and most Islamic practice is aniconic for prophets and angels; represented by calligraphy of the name
deities.summary: Say: the Angel of Death who is set over you will take your souls, then to your Lord you will be returned. ʿAzrāʾīl takes each soul at its appointed time, gently from the believer and harshly from the wrongdoer, acting only by the command of God.

iconography: Not depicted in devotional practice; folklore imagines smoke and flame
deities.summary: God created humankind from clay and the jinn from smokeless fire. Like humans they have free will, are male and female, marry, and will be judged; some heard the Qurʾān and believed, while others follow Iblīs, who was one of the jinn. They were made, like humans, only to worship God.

iconography: Not depicted: Sunni and most Islamic practice is aniconic for prophets and angels; represented by calligraphy of the name
deities.summary: Muḥammad is the Messenger of God and the Seal of the Prophets, sent as a mercy to the worlds, to whom the Qurʾān was revealed. He is not divine and is not worshipped; believers send blessings upon him, follow his example, and hope for his intercession on the Day of Judgment. Sufis honour the Muḥammadan Light, created first of all things, through which the cosmos came to be.
deities.tradition_claim: Venerated, not worshipped: Islam regards Muḥammad as wholly human; listed here as a figure of veneration.

iconography: Not depicted: Sunni and most Islamic practice is aniconic for prophets and angels; represented by calligraphy of the name
deities.summary: Two angels, Hārūt and Mārūt, were sent down at Babylon and taught people sorcery, but never without warning: "We are only a trial, so do not disbelieve." Exegetes tell that they mocked human weakness, were sent to earth with human desires, fell into sin with a woman named Zuhara, and now hang in a pit at Babylon until the Day of Judgment.

deities.etymology: Arabic mālik 'owner, master'.
iconography: Not depicted: Sunni and most Islamic practice is aniconic for prophets and angels; represented by calligraphy of the name
deities.summary: The damned will cry: "O Mālik, let your Lord make an end of us!" He will answer: "You will remain." Mālik is chief of the stern angels set over the Fire, who do not disobey what God commands them.

deities.etymology: Mandaic hiia rbia 'the Great Life'.
deities.summary: In the name of the Great Life! Hayyi Rabbi is the first, the King of Light, from whom all the uthras (beings of light) proceed. The Life dwells in the World of Light, beyond all darkness, and every Mandaean prayer opens in its name.

deities.etymology: Mandaic manda 'knowledge' (cf. Greek gnōsis) d-hiia 'of Life'.
deities.summary: Manda d-Hayyi is the Knowledge of Life, the saviour sent down from the World of Light. He descended to the world of darkness, defeated its powers, brought the soul to Adam, and teaches the elect the way of ascent; Mandaeans take their very name from him.

deities.etymology: Often explained as Egyptian Ptah + -il ('god'); the derivation is proposed, not certain.
deities.summary: Ptahil is the uthra who fashioned the material world, Tibil, and the body of Adam with the help of Ruha and the seven planets. But he could not give life to his creature; the soul had to be brought from the World of Light. For his fault he is barred from the Light until the end, when he will be baptised and restored.

deities.etymology: Aramaic rûḥā 'spirit'; her title Ruha d-Qudsha means 'the Holy Spirit', inverted into a power of darkness.
deities.summary: Ruha is the queen of the world of darkness, mother of Ur and of the seven planets and twelve signs of the zodiac. She helped Ptahil fashion Adam and works to keep souls bound in the body through lust, music and drunkenness, though she sometimes laments her own fallen state.

Abathur sits at the scales at the boundary of the World of Light and weighs every departing soul. From his gaze into the black waters Ptahil came into being. Souls pass through the purgatory houses (matarata) before they are weighed and admitted to the Light.

deities.etymology: Mandaic Hibil = Abel; ziwa 'radiance'.
deities.summary: Hibil Ziwa, the radiant one, descended through the worlds of darkness, overcame their kings, learned their secrets, and brought back Ruha, by whose captivity the powers of darkness were subdued. He returns victorious to the Light as the model of the soul's descent and ascent.
Ur is the gigantic dragon-king of the world of darkness, son of Ruha, who rages against the Light. Hibil Ziwa and the uthras subdue him, and the dead soul must pass him on its way to the scales.

deities.earliest_attestation: 1st c. CE (as a figure); Book of John later
deities.summary: Yahya Yuhana is the great teacher and priest of the Mandaeans, who baptised in the Jordan (yardna) by the power of the Life. He is not the founder of the religion but its greatest prophet, the model of the priest who performs masbuta, living-water baptism.
deities.tradition_claim: Venerated as prophet and priest, not as a god.

primary_sources: Hymn of the Creation (Qewlê Afirîna Dinyayê)
deities.etymology: Kurdish/Persian xwadê 'lord, God'.
deities.summary: Xwedê is the one God who created the world from a pearl and then entrusted its care to the Seven Angels whom he brought forth from his own light. He is beyond the world and is approached through his angels and holy beings.

deities.etymology: Kurdish tawûs 'peacock' + Arabic malik 'king/angel' (malak).
deities.summary: Tawûsî Melek, the Peacock Angel, is the first and chief of the Seven Angels, to whom God gave rule over the world. When God commanded the angels to bow before Adam he refused, for he would bow only to God — and God approved his faithfulness and made him lord of the earth. Yazidis pray facing the sun and honour him with the sacred peacock standard (sancaq).

Sheikh ʿAdī ibn Musāfir came to Lalish and renewed the faith; his tomb at Lalish is the holiest place of the Yazidis, the goal of pilgrimage at the autumn Feast of the Assembly. Yazidis honour him as a manifestation of Tawûsî Melek in human form.

God created seven angels from his light and placed the world in their care; each was later manifest in one of the holy figures of the faith. Tawûsî Melek is first among them, and the seven are honoured as the mysteries through which God governs creation.

Al-Ḥākim, the sixth Fatimid caliph, was the final and complete locus (maqām) in which the One God manifested his unity to humankind. In 1021 he withdrew from sight to test the faithful; at the end of time he will return to establish justice.
deities.tradition_claim: Druze doctrine (secret in its full form); details held by the initiated ʿuqqāl are not public.

deities.summary: Ḥamza ibn ʿAlī is the Imam of the Unitarians and the earthly embodiment of the Universal Intellect, the first being emanated from the One. He proclaimed the Daʿwa in 1017 and wrote many of the Epistles of Wisdom; he too will return with al-Ḥākim at the end.

primary_sources: Gleanings from the Writings of Bahá'u'lláh
deities.summary: God is one, an unknowable essence exalted above every human attribute and comprehension. He reveals himself through a succession of Manifestations — Abraham, Moses, Zoroaster, Krishna, Buddha, Jesus, Muḥammad, the Báb and Bahá'u'lláh — each reflecting his light like a perfect mirror, according to the capacity of the age.

alternate_names: Him Whom God Shall Make Manifest
iconography: Bahá'ís do not display his image publicly; a photograph is viewed only on rare occasions
deities.summary: Bahá'u'lláh is the Manifestation of God for this age, the Promised One of all religions, who declared his mission in the Garden of Riḍván in Baghdad in 1863. He revealed the laws of the Most Holy Book and taught the oneness of God, of religion and of humankind.

The Báb, "the Gate", was the Manifestation of God who declared his mission in Shiraz in 1844, proclaimed himself the promised Qá'im of Islam, and heralded "Him Whom God shall make manifest". He was executed by firing squad in Tabriz in 1850; his shrine stands on Mount Carmel.

ʿAbdu'l-Bahá, eldest son of Bahá'u'lláh, is the Centre of the Covenant, the authorised interpreter of his father's writings and the perfect exemplar of the Bahá'í life. He is not a Manifestation of God, but his servitude is the model for all believers.
deities.tradition_claim: Explicitly not a Manifestation of God in Bahá'í doctrine; listed as a figure of veneration.

deities.summary: The God of Israel is one, the creator who chose Mount Gerizim as the place where his Name dwells (Deuteronomy as preserved by the Samaritans). His Name is not pronounced; it is read as Shema, "the Name".

deities.earliest_attestation: c. 4th c. CE (Memar Marqah) with earlier roots
deities.etymology: Aramaic tāʾēb 'he who returns / restores'.
deities.summary: The Taheb is the prophet like Moses whom God will raise up. He will restore the Divine Favour (Rahuta) that withdrew in the Era of Disfavour (Fanuta), recover the hidden sacred vessels of the Tabernacle on Mount Gerizim, and renew true worship.

alternate_names: Son of the House of God
deities.earliest_attestation: c. 4th c. CE (Memar Marqah) with earlier roots
deities.summary: Moses is the unique prophet, the only one to whom God spoke face to face, the light of the world and the faithful one of God's house. The Samaritan creed confesses one God, Moses his prophet, the Torah, Mount Gerizim and the Day of Vengeance and Recompense.
deities.tradition_claim: Venerated as the unique prophet, not as a god.

deities.etymology: From Hebrew yāh, short form of YHWH, as printed 'JAH' in the King James Version, Psalm 68:4.
deities.summary: Jah is the Most High, the living God, who is present in every person ("I and I") and who revealed himself in the flesh as Haile Selassie I. Rastafari praise Jah through reasoning, Nyabinghi drumming and the chanting down of Babylon.

alternate_names: Conquering Lion of the Tribe of Judah
deities.summary: Haile Selassie I, King of Kings, Lord of Lords, Conquering Lion of the Tribe of Judah, of the line of Solomon and Sheba, is the returned Messiah and the living God revealed. His coronation in 1930 fulfilled prophecy; his visit to Jamaica on 21 April 1966 is celebrated as Grounation Day.

primary_sources: Philosophy and Opinions of Marcus Garvey (1923–25)
deities.summary: Marcus Mosiah Garvey is honoured as the prophet who taught Africans at home and abroad to look to Africa and to God in their own image. His call for repatriation and Black self-reliance prepared the way for the recognition of Haile Selassie.
deities.tradition_claim: Venerated as prophet, not as a god.

primary_sources: The Eleven Satanic Rules of the Earth (1967)
iconography: Sigil of Baphomet (goat head in an inverted pentagram)
deities.summary: Satan is not a being to be worshipped but a symbol: the carnal, proud, self-determining nature of the human animal that religion has condemned. Satan represents indulgence instead of abstinence, vital existence instead of spiritual pipe dreams, and vengeance instead of turning the other cheek. The Satanist is his or her own god; the Infernal Names — Satan, Lucifer, Belial, Leviathan — are invoked in ritual as psychodrama.
deities.tradition_claim: Atheistic: the Church of Satan holds that Satan does not exist as a personal being.

primary_sources: Diverse group-specific texts; no common canon
deities.summary: Satan is a real spiritual being, the liberator who gave humanity knowledge and freedom and who was slandered by the religions of submission. Theistic Satanists honour him through prayer, ritual and devotion as patron, teacher and source of personal power and self-realisation.

Lucifer is the bringer of light, the spirit of illumination, enlightenment and self-deification. Like Prometheus he gave humanity the fire of reason and independent will; the Luciferian walks the path of becoming a self-made light, not a servant.

alternate_names: Satan (as corrupted name, per the Temple)
primary_sources: The Book of Coming Forth by Night (Michael Aquino, 1975)
deities.summary: Set is the Prince of Darkness, the oldest of gods, a real metaphysical being who stands apart from the natural order. He gave humanity the Black Flame — the isolate, self-aware intelligence that sets each mind apart from the universe. Setians do not worship Set but honour him as a friend and model, following the path of Xeper, "to come into being", toward self-created immortality. The Hebrew "Satan" is a later distortion of his name.

primary_sources: The Seven Tenets of The Satanic Temple
Anatole France, The Revolt of the Angels (1914, as literary source)
deities.summary: Satan is a literary symbol, not a deity: the eternal rebel against arbitrary authority, the champion of reason, bodily autonomy, compassion and the pursuit of knowledge. Satanists embrace the name of the Adversary as a declaration of independence from tyranny and superstition.
deities.tradition_claim: Non-theistic: The Satanic Temple does not believe in a supernatural Satan.

deities.summary: Baphomet, winged and goat-headed, sits enthroned with two children gazing up at him: the reconciliation of opposites, of animal and human, male and female, and a symbol of pluralism and open inquiry. The Temple sets him beside monuments to other faiths in public squares to defend religious liberty.

primary_sources: Éliphas Lévi, Dogme et Rituel de la Haute Magie (1854–56), frontispiece "Baphomet du Temple"
Records of the Trial of the Templars (1307–1312)
deities.summary: Baphomet is the hieroglyph of the Great Magical Agent, the astral light: a winged, goat-headed androgyne with a torch of intelligence between the horns, a pentagram on the brow, one arm raised (SOLVE) and one lowered (COAGULA), sitting on the globe. It is the synthesis of all opposites — male and female, light and darkness, good and evil — balanced in the hand of the magus.

primary_sources: Liber AL vel Legis (The Book of the Law), 1904
Stele of Revealing (Stele of Ankh-ef-en-Khonsu, Cairo)
deities.summary: "I am Infinite Space, and the Infinite Stars thereof." Nuit is the boundless circumference, the night-sky goddess arched over all things, who calls every man and every woman to her: "Every man and every woman is a star." She gives unimaginable joys on earth and certainty, not faith, in death.

primary_sources: Liber AL vel Legis (The Book of the Law), 1904
Stele of Revealing (Stele of Ankh-ef-en-Khonsu, Cairo)
deities.summary: "I am the flame that burns in every heart of man, and in the core of every star. I am Life, and the giver of Life." Hadit is the infinitely small point at the centre of Nuit's infinite circle, the hidden self and true will within every being; he is complement and lover of Nuit.

primary_sources: Liber AL vel Legis (The Book of the Law), 1904
Stele of Revealing (Stele of Ankh-ef-en-Khonsu, Cairo)
iconography: hawk-headed god enthroned with the solar disk (as on the Stele of Revealing)
deities.summary: Ra-Hoor-Khuit is the crowned and conquering child, the god of war and of vengeance who rules the new Aeon of Horus that began in 1904. He displaces the Aeon of Osiris, the age of the dying god, with the age of the self-realised child whose law is "Do what thou wilt".

primary_sources: Liber AL vel Legis (The Book of the Law), 1904
Stele of Revealing (Stele of Ankh-ef-en-Khonsu, Cairo)
deities.summary: Hoor-paar-kraat is the silent, passive twin of Ra-Hoor-Khuit; together they form the double god Heru-ra-ha. He is the Lord of Silence, the babe in the egg of spirit, whom Aiwass serves as minister.

deities.etymology: Crowley's spelling of Babylon, taken from the angelic communications he worked through in 1909.
deities.summary: Babalon is the Great Mother, the Scarlet Woman who rides the Beast and holds the cup filled with the blood of the saints: the ecstatic, liberated feminine who receives all things into herself. The adept who pours every drop of his blood into her cup crosses the Abyss and becomes a Master of the Temple in the City of the Pyramids.

primary_sources: Liber AL vel Legis (The Book of the Law), 1904
Stele of Revealing (Stele of Ankh-ef-en-Khonsu, Cairo)
deities.summary: Aiwass is the praeterhuman intelligence who dictated The Book of the Law to Aleister Crowley in Cairo on 8, 9 and 10 April 1904, speaking as the "minister of Hoor-paar-kraat". Crowley later identified him as his own Holy Guardian Angel.
To Mega Therion, the Great Beast, is the title of Aleister Crowley as the prophet of the Aeon of Horus, chosen to receive the Law and to proclaim it to the world with his consort the Scarlet Woman.
deities.tradition_claim: Thelemites regard Crowley as prophet, not god.

primary_sources: The Charge of the Goddess (Doreen Valiente, from Gardnerian Book of Shadows)
Aradia, or the Gospel of the Witches (Charles Godfrey Leland, 1899)
deities.summary: "I who am the beauty of the green earth and the white moon among the stars." The Goddess is the Great Mother of all life, known by countless names — Artemis, Astarte, Diana, Melusine, Aphrodite, Cerridwen, Arianrhod, Isis, Bride. She is Maiden, Mother and Crone, the moon in its phases; "all acts of love and pleasure are my rituals."

alternate_names: the Oak King and Holly King
deities.summary: The Horned God is the Lord of the wild, of animals, the hunt, death and rebirth, consort and son of the Goddess. He is born at Yule, weds the Goddess at Beltane, dies at harvest and rules the summerland of the dead until he is born again: the turning of the Wheel of the Year.

"What is God? God is the supreme intelligence, the first cause of all things." God is eternal, immutable, immaterial, unique, all-powerful, sovereignly just and good. He created spirits simple and ignorant, to progress through many incarnations toward perfection.

primary_sources: The Gospel According to Spiritism (1864), ch. 6
deities.summary: The Consoler promised by Jesus has come as the Spirit of Truth: the collective revelation of the higher spirits who teach the meaning of Christ's words in plain terms. Spiritism itself is the fulfilment of that promise, and messages signed "The Spirit of Truth" guide the work.

primary_sources: Science and Health with Key to the Scriptures (Mary Baker Eddy, 1875), esp. p. 465
deities.summary: God is incorporeal, divine, supreme, infinite Mind, Spirit, Soul, Principle, Life, Truth, Love. God is All-in-all, and since God is good and God is All, matter, sin, sickness and death have no true reality; healing comes from understanding this. God is our Father-Mother.

primary_sources: Science and Health with Key to the Scriptures, pp. 332–334
deities.summary: Jesus was the human man; Christ is the divine idea, "the true idea voicing good", the spiritual selfhood that Jesus most fully expressed. The Christ is eternal and still heals today wherever the divine idea is understood.

deities.earliest_attestation: 1870s CE (Bible Students); name of the movement 1931
primary_sources: New World Translation of the Holy Scriptures (1950/1961)
deities.summary: Jehovah is the only true God, one person, not a Trinity, whose name must be known and sanctified. The great issue before the universe is the vindication of his sovereignty, challenged by Satan in Eden; his Kingdom, ruled by Christ since 1914, will soon replace human governments and restore paradise on earth.

Jesus is God's firstborn son and first creation, the Word through whom all other things were made, known in heaven as Michael the Archangel. He gave his perfect life as a ransom, was raised as a spirit, and has ruled as King of God's Kingdom since 1914, when he cast Satan out of heaven.

God is one person, the Father, and not three. Jesus is a human being exalted by God, the teacher and exemplar of the way to God, but not God himself. Later Unitarian Universalism opened this into a non-creedal free search for truth.

alternate_names: Our Lady of the Covenant of Mercy
deities.earliest_attestation: medieval Ethiopia (Taʾammera Maryam, "Miracles of Mary", 15th c. CE)
deities.summary: Kidane Mehret is the Covenant of Mercy that Christ made with his mother Mary: that whoever calls on her name, honours her memory or gives in her name will receive mercy. On the feast of Kidane Mehret the faithful celebrate this covenant and seek her intercession.

facets.core_claim: In Job and Zechariah the satan is the court's prosecutor: he questions whether human piety is sincere and brings charges before God, and acts only within the limits God sets.
facets.scholarly_note: The definite article (ha-satan) marks a title or office, not a personal name; a personal Satan emerges only in the Second Temple period.

facets.facet_name: The One Who Stands in the Way
facets.core_claim: A satan is whoever blocks the path: the angel of YHWH stands as a satan before Balaam, and in Chronicles a satan incites David to number Israel.
facets.scholarly_note: 1 Chronicles 21:1 rewrites 2 Samuel 24:1, where YHWH himself incites David; the change is widely read as the start of shifting evil impulses away from God.

facets.core_claim: Each nation has its heavenly prince; Michael is Israel's, contending against the princes of Persia and Greece.

facets.facet_name: He Who Arises at the End
facets.core_claim: At the end Michael arises to deliver God's people, an event joined to the resurrection of the dead (Daniel 12:1–2).
Gabriel is sent to give understanding: he interprets visions and announces what God has decreed.
The Angel carries God's own Name and authority; to meet him is to meet God in a form that can be borne.
facets.scholarly_note: The blurred line between YHWH and his angel is a classic problem; see Michael S. Heiser, The Unseen Realm (2015), on the "two powers" reading.

facets.facet_name: The Sea Dragon Crushed by God
facets.core_claim: God broke the heads of Leviathan in the primordial battle and will slay him at the end of days; he embodies the hostile sea that only God can master.

facets.facet_name: The Creature God Made to Play
facets.core_claim: In Psalm 104 and Job 41 Leviathan is no rival but a creature: magnificent, untameable by man, yet God's plaything.

facets.facet_name: Food of the Righteous at the End
facets.core_claim: In the age to come Leviathan and Behemoth will be served as food to the righteous.
Behemoth is the land counterpart to Leviathan: a mighty creature of the first days, mastered only by God and destined to be eaten at the end.
By his power God stilled the sea and by his understanding struck down Rahab; the victory over her is the victory that founds the world.

facets.facet_name: The Star Who Would Be Most High
facets.core_claim: The Day Star sought to raise his throne above El's stars on the divine mountain and was cast down to the Pit: the archetype of hubris against the Most High.
facets.scholarly_note: In context a taunt-song against a Babylonian king that appears to reuse a Canaanite myth of a morning-star deity's failed ascent; see Mark S. Smith, The Origins of Biblical Monotheism (2001).

facets.core_claim: Litan belongs to the host of Yam, the hostile sea, and is slain by Baal and Anat so that the storm-king may rule.
Kings sent to the god of Ekron to learn whether they would recover; he is a Baal who speaks through his oracle.
facets.scholarly_note: "Lord of the Flies" may be a deliberate Hebrew deformation of zbl bʿl, "Baal the Prince", a title of Baal Hadad at Ugarit; the Gospels' Beelzeboul preserves the -l ending.

facets.core_claim: At the Topheth outside Jerusalem the faithless offered their children by fire to the King; the Torah condemns the rite as the defilement of God's name.
facets.scholarly_note: Whether mlk names a god or a type of sacrifice (Punic molk, attested in Carthaginian tophet inscriptions) is debated; Milton later made Moloch a fallen angel.

facets.core_claim: Shahar is the morning: born of El, twin to the evening god Shalim, the bringer of the new day.

facets.facet_name: The Pretender Who Could Not Fill the Throne
facets.core_claim: Athtar ascends the divine mountain to take the vacant throne, proves too small for it, and descends to rule the earth: a would-be king of heaven brought low.
facets.scholarly_note: Cognate with Akkadian Ishtar and South Arabian ʿAthtar, where the deity is the Venus-star; many scholars see the Isaiah 14 Day Star myth behind this episode (Mark S. Smith, The Early History of God).

facets.facet_name: Commander of the Sons of Darkness
facets.core_claim: Belial rules the dominion of wickedness for an appointed time; all who walk in darkness belong to his lot until the final war.
Belial catches Israel in three nets dressed up as righteousness: fornication, wealth and defilement of the temple.
God leaves one tenth of the evil spirits under Mastema's command, so that humans may be tested and punished.
It is Prince Mastema who challenges God to test Abraham's faithfulness by commanding the sacrifice of Isaac, as the satan challenges God over Job.
Raphael heals the blind, drives out demons, and heals the earth itself after the corruption of the Watchers.
Raphael binds Azazel in Dudael and pursues Asmodeus to Upper Egypt where he binds him.
Uriel reveals the true courses of the sun and moon so that the righteous may keep the correct calendar.
Uriel is "over the world and over Tartarus", the angel who shows Enoch the prison of the stars that transgressed.

facets.facet_name: The Jealous Demon of the Bridal Chamber
facets.core_claim: Asmodeus slays the bridegroom out of desire for the bride and is put to flight only by the remedy God reveals through his angel.
In rabbinic legend Ashmedai rules the demons, knows the secret of the shamir, and briefly usurps Solomon's throne.

facets.facet_name: The Wicked One, Chief of the Satans
facets.core_claim: Samael heads the satans; he rode the serpent into Eden and works to bring accusations against Israel before God.
Samael is the angel of death who comes for each soul, filled with eyes, with a drawn sword dripping gall.
facets.scholarly_note: The Talmud (Bava Batra 16a) records Resh Lakish: "Satan, the evil inclination and the angel of death are one."

facets.core_claim: In Kabbalah Samael and Lilith rule the Other Side, the husks (qelippot) that mirror the holy emanations.
facets.scholarly_note: Developed in 13th-c. Castilian Kabbalah; see Gershom Scholem, Major Trends in Jewish Mysticism (1941).

facets.core_claim: Sandalphon gathers the prayers of the faithful and binds them as crowns for God; he spans earth and the highest heaven.
facets.scholarly_note: Later Kabbalah identifies Sandalphon with the transfigured Elijah, as Metatron is the transfigured Enoch.

facets.core_claim: Satan tempts humanity to sin as he tempted Christ, and accuses the brethren before God day and night until he is thrown down.

Satan was created good, rebelled out of pride, and was cast out of heaven with the angels who followed him; in the Life of Adam and Eve he falls because he refuses to worship the image of God in Adam.
For a time Satan holds sway as ruler of this world and prince of the power of the air, blinding unbelievers — until his judgment at the end of the age.

facets.facet_name: The Brightest Angel Cast Down for Pride
facets.core_claim: Lucifer, first among the angels, sought to set his throne above the stars of God; for that pride he fell from light into darkness and became Satan.
facets.scholarly_note: The Vulgate also uses lucifer for the morning star that rises in believers' hearts (2 Peter 1:19), and the Exsultet calls Christ the true Lucifer; the word only gradually became a proper name of the Devil.

facets.core_claim: Beelzebul commands the demons that possess and afflict people; Christ's exorcisms show that his house has been entered and his goods plundered.
The Spirit is fully God, co-eternal with the Father and the Son, the breath of life by whom all things are given life and sanctified.
facets.scholarly_note: East and West divide over whether the Spirit proceeds from the Father alone or from the Father "and the Son" (filioque, added in the West from the 6th c.).

facets.core_claim: Christ promises another Advocate, the Spirit of Truth, who will remain with the disciples, teach them all things and remind them of all he said.

facets.facet_name: Captain of the Hosts Who Casts Down the Dragon
facets.core_claim: When war broke out in heaven, Michael and his angels fought the dragon and threw him down; he is the champion of God against Satan.
Michael receives the souls of the dying, weighs them, and defends them against the Accuser at the hour of death.
Gabriel brings God's decisive announcements, above all the Incarnation of the Word in Mary's womb.

facets.facet_name: The Counterfeit Christ of the End
facets.core_claim: The Antichrist imitates Christ — a death-wound healed, worship demanded, signs performed — in order to lead the world astray before the Second Coming.
Abaddon rules the locust-host of the abyss and is destruction itself, released for an appointed time at the end.
facets.scholarly_note: In the Hebrew Bible ʾăbaddôn is a place — "Destruction", paired with Sheol and Death; Revelation personifies it.

facets.core_claim: Abrasax presides over the full round of heavens, his name containing the number of the year; through it the cosmos is ordered and the initiate gains protection.
facets.scholarly_note: On magical gems he appears as the "anguipede": cock-headed, armoured, with serpent legs. Sethian texts make Abrasax a positive luminary servant rather than an archon.

facets.core_claim: Every revelation to every prophet came through Jibrīl; he carried the Qurʾān from God to Muḥammad over twenty-three years.
Mīkāʾīl directs the rain, plants and provision by which God sustains His creatures.
When God commands, Isrāfīl will blow the Trumpet that ends the world and then the blast that raises the dead.
facets.scholarly_note: The Qurʾān mentions the Trumpet but does not name its angel; the name comes from ḥadīth and later tradition.

facets.core_claim: ʿAzrāʾīl gathers the souls of the dying at their decreed moment and delivers them to the angels of mercy or of punishment.
facets.scholarly_note: The name ʿAzrāʾīl is not Qurʾānic; it appears in later tradition.

facets.core_claim: The jinn are a hidden creation parallel to humanity — believers and unbelievers, righteous and wicked — able to see us where we cannot see them.
Muḥammad completes the chain of prophets from Adam through Abraham, Moses and Jesus; with him revelation is sealed.

facets.facet_name: The Intercessor on the Day of Judgment
facets.core_claim: When all others hold back, the Prophet will prostrate beneath the Throne and be granted intercession for his community.
In Sufi teaching the Reality of Muḥammad (al-ḥaqīqa al-muḥammadiyya) is the first thing God brought forth, the prototype of creation and of the Perfect Human.
facets.scholarly_note: Sufi doctrine (islam-sufi), not shared by all Sunni scholars; the Prophet remains fully human and a creature.

facets.facet_name: The Angels Who Taught Sorcery at Babylon
facets.core_claim: They taught the magic that separates husband from wife as a test; in the exegetical story their descent and fall become a warning about angelic pride.
Mālik guards Hell and its nineteen keepers, carrying out God's justice on the condemned without mercy or disobedience.
Life itself, the infinite Light, is the source from which the worlds of light emanate; it is untouched by matter and darkness.
Manda d-Hayyi comes down from the Light to awaken souls imprisoned in the body and lead them back to the Life.
Ptahil builds the earth and the human body but cannot give them life; his work is real yet flawed, and he must await forgiveness.

facets.facet_name: Mother of the Planets and Lady of Darkness
facets.core_claim: Ruha gives birth to the planetary rulers and labours to hold humanity in the world below the Light.
At Abathur's scales the soul is weighed; only the pure pass on to the Life.
Hibil Ziwa goes down into the depths, binds the powers of darkness and returns in triumph to the World of Light.
Ur is the monster of the dark waters whose rage threatens the Light; he is bound but not destroyed until the end.
Yahya baptised thousands in living water and taught the way of the Life; Mandaeans repeat his baptism weekly.

facets.facet_name: The Creator Who Entrusted the World to His Angels
facets.core_claim: God made the world and delegated its governance to the Seven Angels, chief of whom is Tawûsî Melek.

facets.facet_name: Chief of the Seven Angels, Ruler of the World
facets.core_claim: God set Tawûsî Melek over the world; he governs it and mediates between God and humankind.

facets.facet_name: The Angel Who Bowed Only to God
facets.core_claim: His refusal to bow to Adam was not rebellion but loyalty to the one God, and it was vindicated.
facets.scholarly_note: Neighbouring Muslims and Christians identified him with Iblīs/Satan because of this motif; Yazidis reject the identification, which has fuelled persecution.

facets.facet_name: Saint of Lalish, Manifestation of the Peacock Angel
facets.core_claim: Sheikh ʿAdī is the holy reformer through whom Tawûsî Melek appeared on earth; to visit his tomb is to come to the centre of the world.
facets.scholarly_note: Historically a Sufi of Umayyad descent from the Beqaa valley; his order later developed into the Yazidi religion.

facets.core_claim: The world is ruled by seven angels emanated from God's light, each with his human manifestation.
facets.scholarly_note: Some published lists (from the disputed "Black Book") give them names of the Islamic archangels — Jibrāʾīl, Mīkāʾīl, Isrāfīl, ʿAzrāʾīl, Dardāʾīl, Shamnāʾīl, Nūrāʾīl.

facets.facet_name: The Final Locus of the Divine Unity
facets.core_claim: The unknowable One showed himself in human form through al-Ḥākim, as an image in a mirror shows the face without containing it.

facets.facet_name: The Withdrawn Lord Who Will Return
facets.core_claim: Al-Ḥākim did not die but went into concealment; his return will mark the triumph of the Unitarians.
From the One proceeds the Universal Intellect, and Ḥamza is its human manifestation, chief of the five cosmic ministers.
No one can know God's essence; humanity knows him only through his Manifestations and his attributes reflected in creation.

facets.facet_name: The Manifestation of God for This Age
facets.core_claim: Bahá'u'lláh is a perfect mirror of God's attributes, the latest in the line of Manifestations, bringing laws for a united world.

facets.facet_name: The Promised One of All Ages
facets.core_claim: He fulfils the expectations of every faith: the return of Christ in the glory of the Father, the Shah Bahram of the Zoroastrians, the Lord of Hosts, the Maitreya of the Buddhists.
The Báb is both an independent Manifestation and the forerunner of Bahá'u'lláh, opening a new cycle of revelation.

facets.facet_name: Centre of the Covenant and Perfect Exemplar
facets.core_claim: Through ʿAbdu'l-Bahá the community remained united after Bahá'u'lláh, and in him believers see the teachings lived.

facets.facet_name: The One God Who Chose Mount Gerizim
facets.core_claim: God gave the Torah through Moses and chose Gerizim — not Jerusalem — as the place of his worship.

facets.facet_name: The Restorer of the Era of Favour
facets.core_claim: The Taheb will bring back the age of divine favour and reveal the hidden Tabernacle vessels on Gerizim.
No prophet arose like Moses; through him alone the Law was given, and belief in him is an article of faith.

facets.facet_name: The Living Most High, Present in I and I
facets.core_claim: Jah is God in heaven and within each person, the one whose name the Psalms proclaim.

facets.facet_name: The Returned Messiah and King of Kings
facets.core_claim: In Haile Selassie the promised Christ returned in kingly character, the Lion of Judah who opens the seals.
facets.scholarly_note: Haile Selassie himself was a devout Ethiopian Orthodox Christian and did not claim divinity; Rastafari reject reports of his death in 1975.

facets.core_claim: Garvey, like Moses, called a scattered people to return to the promised land of Africa.
facets.scholarly_note: The famous prophecy "Look to Africa, when a black king shall be crowned" is attributed to him by Rastafari; it is not found in his published writings.

facets.facet_name: Satan as Symbol of the Carnal Self
facets.core_claim: Satan stands for everything that is natural in humanity — pride, desire, rational self-interest — and for opposition to the spiritual tyranny of the herd.

facets.facet_name: The Four Crown Princes of Hell
facets.core_claim: In Satanic ritual the four quarters are given to the Crown Princes of Hell: Satan (south, fire), Lucifer (east, air), Belial (north, earth) and Leviathan (west, water).

facets.facet_name: Satan as Real Patron and Liberator
facets.core_claim: The Adversary of the Bible is a real and benevolent power whose rebellion against the tyrant-god opened the way to knowledge and freedom.
Lucifer is the principle of illumination: the will to know, to question and to become one's own light.

facets.facet_name: The Prince of Darkness, Giver of the Black Flame
facets.core_claim: Set is the principle of isolate consciousness; his gift of the Black Flame lets the individual stand apart from nature and create itself.
Set's word is Xeper: the Setian's endless self-creation and self-development.

facets.facet_name: The Eternal Rebel Against Arbitrary Authority
facets.core_claim: Satan embodies the refusal to bow to unjust power and the insistence on reason and conscience.

facets.facet_name: Emblem of Reconciled Opposites and Pluralism
facets.core_claim: Baphomet stands for the balance of opposites and the right of every conscience to stand in the public square.
Baphomet is not the Devil but the image of the universal agent through which all magic works: solve et coagula, the balance of opposites.
facets.scholarly_note: The name appears first in 14th-c. accusations that the Templars worshipped an idol; it is most likely a garbling of "Mahomet". Lévi's 1856 drawing created the now-standard image.

facets.core_claim: Nuit is the totality of possibility, infinitely extended; every star — every individual — is a point within her body.

facets.facet_name: The Point at the Core of Every Star
facets.core_claim: Hadit is the core of each individual, the secret self who experiences Nuit's infinity; their union is the source of all.

facets.facet_name: Crowned and Conquering Child, Lord of the Aeon
facets.core_claim: Ra-Hoor-Khuit is the active, solar Horus enthroned over the new age; his law is Thelema, will.
Hoor-paar-kraat is the inward, silent aspect of the god of the Aeon, the stillness from which will acts.

facets.facet_name: The Scarlet Woman and Holy Grail
facets.core_claim: Babalon is the sacred harlot of the Aeon, the cup of total surrender through which the initiate dissolves the ego and crosses the Abyss.

facets.facet_name: The Angel Who Dictated the Law
facets.core_claim: Through Aiwass the new Law was delivered word for word; he is the messenger of the gods of the Aeon.

facets.facet_name: The Beast, Prophet of the New Aeon
facets.core_claim: The Beast is the prophet through whom the Word of the Aeon, Thelema, is uttered.

facets.facet_name: The Great Mother of Many Names
facets.core_claim: All goddesses are one Goddess, mother of nature and of all living souls, worshipped at the full moon.
The Goddess shows three faces as the moon waxes, is full and wanes: youth, motherhood and wisdom.

facets.facet_name: Lord of Beasts and the Hunt
facets.core_claim: The Horned God is the vital power of animal life and the green world, the hunter and the hunted.

facets.facet_name: The God Who Dies and Is Reborn
facets.core_claim: Through the year the God is born, weds, dies and returns, guiding the dead to rest and rebirth.

facets.facet_name: The Supreme Intelligence and First Cause
facets.core_claim: God is the first cause; every effect has a cause, and the intelligence behind the universe is God, who leads all spirits to perfection.
The Spirit of Truth fulfils Christ's promise by revealing the immortality of the soul, reincarnation and the law of love.
God is the only Mind and the only reality; whatever is unlike God is illusion, dispelled by spiritual understanding.
The Comforter promised by Christ is Divine Science, the spiritual law that heals as Jesus healed.
The Christ is the spiritual idea of God that came to the flesh to destroy incarnate error; Jesus demonstrated it.

facets.facet_name: The Universal Sovereign Whose Name Must Be Sanctified
facets.core_claim: Jehovah alone is Almighty; history is the vindication of his rightful sovereignty.

facets.facet_name: Holy Spirit as God's Active Force
facets.core_claim: The holy spirit is not a person but Jehovah's active force, by which he creates and empowers his servants.

facets.facet_name: The Firstborn Son, Michael the Archangel
facets.core_claim: Before coming to earth Jesus was Michael, the chief of the angels; he is God's son and agent, but not God Almighty.
Scripture and reason show one God, the Father; the doctrine of the Trinity is a later human invention.
Through the covenant Christ gave her, Mary intercedes and obtains mercy for all who invoke her.

basis: The court accuser of Job and Zechariah becomes the personal Accuser of Revelation 12:10 who accuses the brethren before God
Septuagint renders śāṭān as diabolos, the source of "devil"
Both test human fidelity before God
parallels.scholarly_caveat: The Hebrew Bible satan is a subordinate functionary, not God's cosmic enemy; the shift is gradual across the Second Temple period.

basis: Arabic shayṭān is cognate with Hebrew śāṭān and was likely transmitted through Aramaic/Ethiopic usage
Both accuse and test humanity under God's permission
Jubilees makes Mastema provoke God to test Abraham as the satan provokes God to test Job
Both act only with divine permission
Both are named from the root "hostility/opposition"
In Numbers 22 the Angel of YHWH himself stands "as a satan" against Balaam
Shows satan as a role an envoy of God can fill
The War Scroll says God made Belial "for the pit, an angel of mastema (hostility)"
Both lead the evil spirits that test and harm Israel for a fixed time
Paul uses Beliar as the opposite of Christ, i.e. as a name for Satan
Both rule the present age of darkness until defeated
The Community Rule's two spirits of truth and deceit resemble the Zoroastrian twin spirits
Both lead a camp of darkness opposed to the camp of light until a final victory
parallels.scholarly_caveat: Persian influence on Qumran dualism is a hypothesis; the Qumran spirits are both created by God, unlike Zoroastrian Angra Mainyu.

basis: A cosmic adversary who rules or corrupts the world for a limited age
Both are defeated in a final eschatological battle
parallels.scholarly_caveat: Possible Persian influence on Jewish and Christian demonology after the exile is debated; the Christian Devil remains a creature, not an independent principle.

basis: In the Life of Adam and Eve Satan is cast out for refusing to worship Adam; the Qurʾān tells the same of Iblīs
Both fall through pride at the creation of humanity
Iblīs is commonly derived from Greek diabolos; al-Shayṭān from śāṭān
Both tempt humanity to disobey God until the Day of Judgment
parallels.scholarly_caveat: Islam presents Iblīs as one of the jinn rather than a fallen angel in most readings.

basis: Jerome's Vulgate translates Hebrew hêlēl as "lucifer"
The fall from heaven for wanting to be like the Most High is carried over intact
A star-god attempts to take the throne on Zaphon, the divine mountain in the north
He fails and descends to rule below (earth / Sheol)
parallels.scholarly_caveat: The connection is widely argued but not certain; Mark S. Smith, The Early History of God.

basis: Origen and later fathers read Isaiah 14 as the fall of the Devil
Lucifer becomes the pre-fall name of Satan
"I will be like the Most High" parallels the archon's boast "I am God and there is no other"
Both are powers whose pride over-reaches the true God
The same Morning Star figure, revalued from proud rebel to liberator
Luciferians read the fall as an act of illumination
parallels.syncretic_source: Modern Luciferianism (late 20th c.) reinterpreting the Christian Lucifer
parallels.scholarly_caveat: Christian tradition sees the same act as the origin of evil.

basis: A light/fire-bringer who gives humanity knowledge against the will of the sovereign god
Punished or demonised for that gift
ʿAthtar is the Semitic cognate of Ishtar
Both are tied to the Venus star in parts of their range
parallels.scholarly_caveat: Cognate names, but the Ugaritic Athtar is male and has a different mythic role.

basis: Personified Dawn who opens the day
Born of the high gods and paired with the evening
The Gospels' Beelzeboul is the god of Ekron renamed as prince of demons
The Hebrew deformation "lord of flies" is preserved in the variant Beelzebub
Jesus answers the charge "by Beelzebul" with "if Satan casts out Satan", treating them as one
Both command the demons
zbl bʿl, "Baal the Prince", is a title of Baal Hadad at Ugarit
Baal Zebub is a local Baal of Ekron consulted for healing
parallels.scholarly_caveat: Whether Ekron's god was Hadad or a distinct local Baal is uncertain.

basis: Rabbinic texts call Samael "chief of all the satans" and make him the tempter in Eden
The Ascension of Isaiah uses Sammael alongside Satan and Beliar for the same ruler of this world
Gnostic texts give Samael as a name of the chief archon
Hypostasis of the Archons glosses Samael as "god of the blind"
parallels.scholarly_caveat: The Gnostic usage borrows a Jewish angel name and reverses its target onto the creator.

basis: Kabbalistic texts pair Samael and Lilith as king and queen of the demonic realm
Both seduce and endanger humans
Samael rules the qelippot, the Sitra Achra that mirrors the holy sefirot
Both define a dark counterpart to the divine emanations
Both are the angel of death who takes each soul at its appointed time
Both act strictly under God's command
Islamic exegesis gives Iblīs's name before his fall as ʿAzāzīl
Both are rebellious angelic figures expelled from heaven
parallels.scholarly_caveat: The name ʿAzāzīl is reported in exegetical traditions (e.g. from Ibn ʿAbbās) and is not in the Qurʾān; the roles differ.

basis: Both are bound by Raphael in a desert place (Dudael; Upper Egypt)
Both are destructive spirits neutralised by angelic binding
Raphael is the agent of the binding that is Azazel's fate
The same scene seen from binder and bound
Both refuse to bow before Adam out of loyalty/pride toward God alone
Yazidism vindicates the refusal; Islam condemns it
parallels.scholarly_caveat: The shared motif is the root of outsiders' identification of Tawûsî Melek with Iblīs, which Yazidis reject.

basis: Both are angelic rulers of this world
Outsiders equated the Peacock Angel with Satan; Yazidis venerate him as God's faithful chief angel
parallels.syncretic_source: Polemical identification by Muslim and Christian neighbours and 19th-c. Western travellers; rejected by Yazidis
parallels.scholarly_caveat: A polemical misidentification, not a Yazidi teaching; it has been used to justify persecution, including the 2014 genocide.

basis: Yazidis hold that Tawûsî Melek appeared in human form as Sheikh ʿAdī
Both are the centre of Yazidi devotion at Lalish
The Temple worships the same Egyptian Set, keeping the name Sutekh
It values the outsider-adversary qualities that Egyptian myth gave him
parallels.syncretic_source: Temple of Set, founded by Michael Aquino, 1975 (The Book of Coming Forth by Night)
parallels.scholarly_caveat: Egyptian Set was also a protector of Ra; the Setian reading draws selectively on his adversary role.

basis: The Temple holds that "Satan" is a Hebrew distortion of the name Set
Both are the Prince of Darkness who sets himself apart from the cosmic order
parallels.syncretic_source: Temple of Set, founded by Michael Aquino, 1975
parallels.scholarly_caveat: The etymology Set → Satan is a Setian claim; linguists derive śāṭān from a Hebrew root meaning "oppose".

basis: The Temple of Set split from the Church of Satan in 1975
It kept the LaVeyan emphasis on self-deification but made the Prince of Darkness a real being
parallels.source_tradition: Church of Satan → Temple of Set (1975 schism)

basis: A venerated adversary who gives humanity self-aware illumination
Both frame the path as self-deification
LaVey took the Christian Adversary as a symbol and inverted its valuation
The Satanic Bible's Infernal Names come from Christian demonology
Same name and adversarial role
LaVeyans treat Satan as a symbol; theistic Satanists as a real being
Theistic Satanists hold that the being they venerate is the biblical Satan
The fall is reread as liberation rather than sin
parallels.scholarly_caveat: Christian theology regards the same being as wholly evil.

basis: Both are non-theistic: Satan as symbol, not being
The Satanic Temple emphasises the rebel against tyranny, LaVeyans the carnal self
The rebel who defies an arbitrary sovereign for the sake of humanity
Both are literary heroes of the Romantic tradition of rebellion
The Satanic Temple's bronze is modelled directly on Lévi's 1856 Baphomet
Both depict the winged goat-headed androgyne as union of opposites
primary_text_evidence: Dogme et Rituel de la Haute Magie (frontispiece)

basis: The Church of Satan's Sigil of Baphomet uses the goat head of Lévi's figure within an inverted pentagram
The goat-image migrates from occult symbol to Satanic emblem
parallels.scholarly_caveat: Lévi insisted Baphomet was not the Devil.

basis: Horned, goat- or stag-headed figure of nature's power
Both are read as symbols of balance and vitality rather than evil
The horned Devil of Christian art and the horned god share an iconography partly derived from Pan
Wiccans reject the identification of their God with Satan
parallels.scholarly_caveat: The early-20th-c. theory that the witch trials' "Devil" was a surviving horned god is rejected by historians.

basis: Isaiah 27:1 repeats the Ugaritic epithets "fleeing serpent, twisting serpent" word for word
The names ltn and liwyātān are the same word
The sea-dragon whose defeat founds cosmic order
Divine warrior splits/crushes the monster of the waters
Hostile sea defeated by the storm/divine warrior
Psalm 74 joins the splitting of Yam (sea) with the crushing of Leviathan
Litan belongs to Yam's host of the sea
Both are slain by Baal and Anat
Revelation's seven-headed dragon, "the ancient serpent", reuses the Leviathan image for Satan
Both are slain/bound by God at the end
The sea monster cut in pieces at creation
Cosmic order established by the divine warrior's victory
Parallel names for the primordial sea enemy in Isaiah and Job
Both are pierced/crushed by YHWH
Paired primordial beasts of land and sea
Both reserved as food for the righteous at the end
The dragon of the dark waters hostile to the divine
Bound or subdued by the forces of light
Greek writers describe Carthaginian child sacrifice by fire to "Kronos"
Both are associated with the devouring of children
parallels.scholarly_caveat: Greek interpretatio of the Punic Baal Hammon; whether biblical Molech is a god or a rite is debated.

basis: The Carthaginian tophet sacrifices dedicated to Tanit and Baal Hammon match the biblical Topheth rite
Both involve infant offerings recorded as mlk/molk
parallels.scholarly_caveat: Interpretation of the tophet remains contested.

basis: Personified Destruction/Death ruling the underworld
Both devour the living
Both are an end-time deceiver posing as Messiah, slain by Jesus at his return
Arabic dajjāl corresponds to Syriac Christian daggālā "deceiver", used of the Antichrist
Crowley adopted the title To Mega Therion, the Beast 666 of Revelation 13
He inverted the Beast into the prophet of the new Aeon
Babalon is the Whore of Babylon riding the seven-headed beast, revalued as sacred
Cup, beast and scarlet are taken directly from Revelation 17
Jerome notes that both "Abraxas" and "Meithras" add up to 365
Both are tied to the cycle of the year
parallels.scholarly_caveat: An isopsephic coincidence noted in antiquity, not proof of a shared cult.

basis: Composite animal-headed ruler with serpent body
Both preside over the planetary heavens
The great prince of Daniel is the captain of the hosts of Revelation
Both fight God's battles against hostile powers
The Qurʾān names Mīkāl beside Jibrīl as angels brought near
The name is the Arabic form of Mikhaʾel
Divine champion who defeats the dragon and secures heaven
Revelation's war in heaven reuses the combat myth
A heavenly figure who weighs the soul after death
Decides admission to the realm of light
Jehovah's Witnesses hold that the pre-human Jesus is Michael the Archangel
Both lead the heavenly army against Satan
parallels.syncretic_source: Watch Tower Bible and Tract Society (Jehovah's Witnesses), 20th c.
parallels.scholarly_caveat: Mainstream Christianity rejects the identification.

basis: The same Jesus of the New Testament, read as God's first creation rather than co-eternal God
Both are the Word through whom all else was made
parallels.source_tradition: Bible Student movement (C. T. Russell) from Protestant Christianity

basis: The interpreter of Daniel's visions is the angel of the Annunciation
Both announce God's decrees to chosen humans
Jibrīl is the Arabic form of Gavriʾel
The angel of revelation in all three traditions
The Qurʾān calls the bringer of revelation Rūḥ al-Qudus, "the Holy Spirit", which exegetes identify with Jibrīl
Both convey divine revelation to prophets
parallels.scholarly_caveat: Islam does not regard the Spirit as divine; the shared title has different theological meaning.

basis: An angelic intelligence dictates a scripture word for word to a prophet
Revelation in a set place and time (Hira; Cairo 1904)
Divine messenger who carries the decrees of the high god to humans
Mediates between the heavenly court and chosen mortals
Divine healer of blindness and disease
Healing linked to sacred remedy (fish gall; snake and dream)
Heavenly reckoner of the sun, moon and calendar
Reveals the measures of time to scribes
Angel set over the prison of the damned
Executes divine judgment on the condemned
A divine herald whose horn-blast announces the end of the world
Waits in readiness for the final moment
Yazidi lists name the Seven Angels with Islamic archangel names including ʿAzrāʾīl
Shared Islamic angelology
parallels.scholarly_caveat: The named list comes from texts of disputed authenticity.

basis: Jibrāʾīl appears among the Seven Angels in Yazidi lists
Both belong to a council of chief angels under God
parallels.scholarly_caveat: The named list comes from texts of disputed authenticity.

basis: A heptad of divine beings emanated from the high God to govern creation
Each member oversees part of the created order
primary_text_evidence: Yasht 19.16-18 (the seven Amesha Spentas of one mind)
Greater Bundahishn 1 (Ohrmazd creates the six Amesha Spentas)
parallels.scholarly_caveat: Possible Iranian substrate in Yazidism; no direct transmission is proven.

basis: The Talmud applies "my Name is in him" (Exodus 23:21) to Metatron
Both bear the divine Name as God's chief agent
Early Christian writers identified the Angel of the LORD with the pre-incarnate Word
Both make the invisible God visible
parallels.scholarly_caveat: A Christian reading; Jewish tradition does not identify the Angel with a divine person.

basis: Later Kabbalah identifies Sandalphon with the transfigured Elijah, parallel to Enoch becoming Metatron
Both span earth and heaven
parallels.scholarly_caveat: Medieval kabbalistic identification, not Talmudic.

basis: Angels descend to earth, teach magic, and sin with a woman
Bound in a pit until judgment
Invisible intermediate spirits that can afflict humans
A realm of spirits between angels and humanity
The Spirit of God hovering over the waters becomes the third person of the Trinity
Hebrew rûaḥ ha-qōdeš is rendered pneuma hagion
Kardec identified the promised Consoler/Spirit of Truth with Spiritist revelation
Both fulfil John 14:16–26
parallels.syncretic_source: Allan Kardec, The Gospel According to Spiritism (1864)
parallels.scholarly_caveat: Christian churches reject the identification.

basis: Mary Baker Eddy taught that the promised Comforter is Divine Science
Both are the Spirit leading into all truth
parallels.syncretic_source: Mary Baker Eddy, Science and Health (1875)

basis: Mandaean Ruha bears the title Ruha d-Qudsha, "the Holy Spirit"
Mandaeism inverts the Christian Holy Spirit into a power of darkness
parallels.scholarly_caveat: Often read as Mandaean polemic against Christianity.

basis: Same biblical holy spirit
Trinitarians call it a divine person; Jehovah's Witnesses an impersonal force
Jah is the short form of YHWH found in Psalm 68:4 and Hallelu-jah
Same God of Israel, read through the King James Bible
parallels.source_tradition: Rastafari from the King James Bible

basis: "Jehovah" is a Latinised form of YHWH with the vowels of Adonai
Same covenant God, understood as unipersonal
The same Tetragrammaton God of the Pentateuch
Samaritans and Jews share the Torah but dispute the chosen place
Strict unipersonal monotheism rejecting the Trinity
God without partners or co-equals
Non-trinitarian one God, the Father
Jesus subordinate to God
God's essence is unknowable and beyond all attributes
Bahá'í theology grew from Shiʿi Islamic thought
God as first cause and supreme intelligence from which all derives
All beings proceed from and return toward that source
God as the only true reality behind appearances
Union of the soul with the divine ground
parallels.scholarly_caveat: Eddy's idealism and Eckhart's apophatic ground differ substantially.

basis: Eddy's Christ as "divine idea" reinterprets the Johannine Logos
Distinguishes the human Jesus from the eternal Christ
Ibn ʿArabī identifies the Muḥammadan Reality with the Perfect Human
Both are the mirror in which all divine names are manifest
A pre-existent principle through which creation came to be
Manifest in a historical messenger
parallels.scholarly_caveat: Islam rejects any divinity of Muḥammad; the parallel is structural only.

basis: Intercessor whose plea before God obtains mercy for believers
Devotion expressed by invoking blessings on the intercessor's name
The prophet through whom the definitive law is given
Belief in him is an article of faith
Expected end-time restorer who renews true worship and justice
Prophet-like figure, not God
John's Gospel shows a Samaritan woman expecting the Messiah who "will tell us everything"
Both are a coming prophet-redeemer
The Báb proclaimed himself the Qá'im, the promised Mahdi of Shiʿi Islam
Both inaugurate the end-time renewal
parallels.syncretic_source: The Báb (1848 declaration at Tabriz); Bábí and Bahá'í Faiths
parallels.scholarly_caveat: Muslims reject the claim.

basis: Bahá'u'lláh proclaimed himself the return of Christ in the glory of the Father
Both are the promised redeemer of the last age
parallels.scholarly_caveat: Christians reject the claim.

basis: Bahá'ís identify Bahá'u'lláh with the Zoroastrian promised saviour (Shah Bahram)
Both bring the final renovation
parallels.syncretic_source: Bahá'í Faith (writings of Bahá'u'lláh and Shoghi Effendi)
parallels.scholarly_caveat: Zoroastrian orthodoxy rejects the claim.

basis: Bahá'í writings identify Bahá'u'lláh with the coming Buddha Maitreya
Both are the future world-teacher
parallels.scholarly_caveat: Buddhist traditions reject the claim.

basis: Both are prophet-lawgivers in a line from Abraham
Bahá'ís reinterpret "Seal of the Prophets" so that new Manifestations remain possible
parallels.scholarly_caveat: Islam holds prophecy ended with Muḥammad.

basis: Designated successor and authorised interpreter of the founder
Keeps the community united after the founder's death
A Fatimid/Ismaili leader withdraws into concealment and will return at the end
Druze occultation doctrine grows from Shiʿi Imamology
The first emanation from the One is the Universal Intellect
Druze cosmology inherits Ismaili Neoplatonism
Rastafari identify Haile Selassie I as the returned Christ in kingly character
Titles King of Kings and Lion of Judah from Revelation
parallels.syncretic_source: Early Rastafari preachers in Jamaica (Leonard Howell and others), 1930s
parallels.scholarly_caveat: Haile Selassie, an Ethiopian Orthodox Christian, did not claim this; Christian churches reject it.

basis: Leader calling a people out of bondage to a promised land
Popularly called "Black Moses"
The Ethiopian Covenant of Mercy is a form of Marian intercession
Mary obtains mercy for those who invoke her
Sheikh ʿAdī was a Sufi master; Yazidi veneration of him grows from the Sufi saint-pole idea
Both are living axes of divine presence
parallels.scholarly_caveat: Yazidism developed far beyond its Sufi origins.

basis: Withdrawn high god who delegates rule to a council of subordinate powers
The creator stands above the world his agents administer
Transcendent source beyond the material world from which the light-beings emanate
Untouched by the creator of matter
parallels.scholarly_caveat: Mandaeism is related to but distinct from Sethian and Valentinian Gnosticism; see Birger Pearson, Ancient Gnosticism (2007).

basis: Descending revealer who brings saving knowledge from the realm of light
Defeats the powers of darkness and opens the way of ascent for souls
parallels.scholarly_caveat: Mandaeism rejects Jesus; the parallel is the shared Gnostic redeemer pattern.

basis: Lower being who fashions the material world and the body of Adam
Cannot give the soul; life must come from the higher realm
The name Ptahil is often derived from Ptah
Both are craftsman-creators of the world
parallels.scholarly_caveat: Proposed etymology; the Mandaean figure is a flawed demiurge, unlike Ptah.

basis: Fallen feminine power who is mother of the world-rulers
Assists in fashioning humanity's body
Judgment of the dead by weighing at the threshold of the blessed realm
Only the pure soul is admitted to the realm of the blessed
Descent into the underworld to bind its powers and return victorious
The descent opens the way for souls to ascend
Descent through the gates of the underworld and triumphant return
A divine figure confronts the rulers of the dead in their own realm
Nuit is the sky-goddess Nut as shown arching over the Stele of Revealing
Both are the star-filled body of the sky
Hadit is drawn from the winged disk Behdety (Horus of Behdet) on the Stele
Solar-winged emblem of the god
Ra-Hoor-Khuit is the hawk-headed Re-Harakhty enthroned on the Stele of Revealing
Solar king of the gods
The two are the passive and active halves of Heru-ra-ha
Book of the Law presents them as one double god
Harpocrates, Horus the Child son of Isis, is taken over as the Thelemic Lord of Silence
Both are the child-form of Horus
Infinite circumference and infinitely small centre
Divine lovers whose union produces all things
One Goddess of many names, mother of nature
The Charge lists Isis among her names
The Charge of the Goddess names Diana among her names
Leland's Aradia makes Diana queen of the witches
parallels.syncretic_source: Charles Godfrey Leland, Aradia (1899); Gardnerian Wicca and Doreen Valiente's Charge (1950s)

basis: Triple-formed goddess
Tied to the moon, night and magic
parallels.scholarly_caveat: Wiccan Maiden-Mother-Crone is a 20th-c. formulation; Hekate's triple form is ancient but not identical.

basis: Wicca names Cernunnos as a name of the Horned God
Antlered lord of animals and fertility
parallels.scholarly_caveat: Ancient Cernunnos is known mainly from iconography; the Wiccan theology is modern.

basis: God who dies and rises with the agricultural year
Rules the land of the dead between
Wild, horned or animal-linked god of nature and ecstasy
Associated with death and renewal in the cycle of the year
God presents Behemoth and Leviathan side by side as creatures only he can master
Both display divine power over untameable creation
Both are kings of demons whom Solomon commands in the Testament of Solomon
Both rule hosts of afflicting spirits
A historical man held to be the human manifestation of a divine being
Medieval Islamic-world figure transformed by a later esoteric community
parallels.scholarly_caveat: Druze and Yazidi doctrines of manifestation differ and are unrelated historically.
